Prodigiosin production in *S. marcescens* is strongly temperature-dependent: it peaks at **25–28 °C** and is suppressed at **≥37 °C** (p. 2; also illustrated in Fig. 2A, p. 4).

The paper attributes this thermosensitivity in part to decreased expression and stability of the biosynthetic enzymes PigF and PigN at higher temperatures; engineering longer-lived *pigF*/*pigN* mRNAs (via artificial polynucleotide fragments in the 3′ UTRs) and introducing rationally designed disulfide bonds into PigF improved yields at both 30 °C and 37 °C (p. 9). Transcriptional thermoregulation is also noted as involving the repressor HexS (Table 3, p. 11).
question: At what temperature does prodigiosin production peak, and when is it suppressed?
